« I'm ready for the season »

After a summer marked by particularly tense contract negotiations with the Pistons, Jalen Duren made a successful return to the court last night. In his first preseason game, the 22-year-old center scored 24 points on 8/9 shooting and 8/8 from the free-throw line, with 3 rebounds, 2 steals, and 1 block in just 15 minutes, during Detroit's victory over the Wolves (128-106).

« I feel good. I'm just happy to be back with the guys and the staff. It's been a good week. I've been able to find my rhythm, get my bearings, get to know some of the new players. I'm ready for the season. »

Absent from training camp and the first two preseason games, Duren comes off a tumultuous summer. Negotiations with Detroit had notably stalled over a clause related to his weight, which was ultimately removed, before the two sides reached an agreement on a 5-year, $200 million contract.

author: Adam Stock
text:
- The big story in this one was not LeBron's or Brown's debut. It was how bad Embiid looked. In 24 minutes, he put up 6/3/8. That 8 is not his assists. That 8 is his turnovers. He looked every bit as bad as that stat line suggests. That video of him passing on an oop and showing off what looked like a 2-inch vert was pretty shocking as well. That being said...Embiid always looks like hot garbage in the preseason. He's one of those guys who plays himself into shape. He could be cooked, but I don't think tonight tells us that. Unfortunately, we probably won't know until November if he still has much left in the tank. I'm not drafting him anywhere close to his ADP in H2H leagues. Even in Roto, I would want him at a discount. He's still not a great pick in his range in Roto if he gives us 50 games of top-25 numbers. For now, I'm assuming he's still very good on offense but pretty washed on defense. That's mostly going off what we saw last year. That's a bigger problem for the Sixers than his fantasy value.
- LeBron only took one shot but went to the line 8 times. That worked out to a 15.3% usage rate, which is role player-level. It's not going to be that low, but I would be very surprised if he hit 20 PPG this year. The dimes should go up, though. He's another Sixer I'm staying far, far away from at his ADP. I think he's more of a top-60 per-game player this year in nine-cat. He's probably missing 20+ games. You can't take that in the fourth.
- Maxey and Brown both looked sharp. They will be a little inconsistent due to Embiid and James being in and out of the lineup, but I think their final numbers will justify where they are being drafted. I'm good with Maxey in the middle of the first. I'm good with Brown toward the end of the fourth in 12-teamers.
- Edgecombe was solid too. I'm not really shying away from him either. His threes, steals, and minutes give him a pretty solid floor, and there's a good chance that he spends a good chunk of the year as the team's third option.

However, what is definitely notable and exciting about Harper's night is the threes. 3/5 from deep in just 19 minutes. It's nice that they went in, but that would be exciting even if he was 1/5. If Harper is going to be a 1.5+ 3PG player this year, that ups his ceiling a round or two. If he keeps taking them over the rest of the preseason, I would be comfortable going a little above his current ADP. We should keep an eye on his FT% too this preseason. We need him to make a jump there. His steal rate is a big question mark as well. It was surprisingly mediocre last year after being pretty solid at Rutgers. College steal rate is usually a good predictor of NBA steal rate, so last year's performance was unexpected. His college steal rate suggests he has some upside in the category.
- Wemby was a bit quiet, but that doesn't mean much. We should pay very little attention to how stars play in preseason unless they are coming off a big injury or are in a new role.
- I'm not interested in Vassell in 12-team leagues. I don't think he's even all that interesting in 14-team leagues either. He's done as a quality fantasy option as long as he's in SA.

topic: Nets section of a multi-team post
text:
- No Sharpe tonight, so Wagner got the start. He could be a deep league guy if Sharpe goes down at some point.
- No MPJ either, so Clowney started. Zero interest there. He's just not very good, and his game isn't as category league-friendly as it is made out to be. He's not a high-upside guy, even in a big role.
- Ellis is going to start until Brown is back. He's draftable in 14-team leagues and is a nice Week 1 stream in shallower settings. Brown will probably be somewhat limited early.
- Demin had 13 on 13 shots, but I would argue this was an encouraging night because he took 10 shots inside the arc. He only went 4 for 10 on those shots, but for Demin, that is a big improvement. He was one of the worst players in the league inside the arc last year. He played 25 MPG and only took two shots per night from two. I'm not expecting any miracles, but it is nice to see him expand his game, as it gives him a better shot at being more than a punt FG%-only player. That's really the only build I'm targeting him in, but I think as the Nets' likely third option, he could improve enough over the course of the season to be more than that.
- Next to Ellis, Minott is the most interesting of the Nets' likely bench options, but I'm not using a pick on him. Bad players with fantasy-friendly games are usually a trap. We watch and pick him up if he starts to look good.

text:
NBA Preseason Wednesday Night Notes

The only real situation I'm monitoring in Phoenix is Oso vs. Maluach for center minutes. Oso played 17 and started, going 8-2-2 with a steal. Maluach played 25 min off the bench, finishing with 8-7-4, no threes or blocks.  

I'm resetting expectations for Maluach a bit, but he's still the guy to roster. Oso just doesn't do much with his minutes and will always be the fifth option, no matter who he's out there with.

For the Bulls, Caleb Wilson (6-16) and Matas Buzelis (6-15) were wildly inefficient, combining to shoot 0-10 from three. It's good to see the volume there, and the shooting is bound to be better. Matas had 2 steals and 2 blocks. Still love him as a breakout, and Wilson oozes upside, but is going to have some rough nights, as all rookies do.

OKC studs looked great, and I like J-Dub for a bounceback year. Cason Wallace is a nice late-round value for steals as well. 

Aday Mara went nuts and looks tremendous, but he's just not going to play this year much unless Chet or Hartenstein are out. 

Jared McCain got up 11 shots in 16 minutes; he's still on my radar even though Ajay Mitchell is the bench guy we really want and a spot starter on nights that OKC starters are rested or hurt.

Kel'el Ware started at the four alongside Turner and had a very nice line of 18-12 with a block. Turner, FWIW, had 19-5 with 3 stocks and is a potential value late in drafts, too. 

Will they use this lineup in the regular season? They should, but even if Ware comes off the bench, he's still a breakout candidate and a target in the middle rounds.

Brayden Burries went 16-5-1 with 2 steals and is a guy I love in dynasty, though I'm not sure he'll have a large role this year unless Milwaukee moves a guard ahead of him.

The Magic starters didn't play much, other than Jase Richardson, who started for Suggs. Tristan da Silva put up a 19-5-2 line but on 6-for-16 shooting. He was solid as a fill-in last season, but isn't really draftable with Orlando at full strength.

Ty Jerome scored 17 points on 14 shots in 19 minutes. He's still a value late in drafts, but for how long? Feels like he's being touted EVERYWHERE. 

Boozer was solid with 16-6-2, while GG Jackson went off for 15 points in 13 minutes off the bench. He's a guy to keep an eye on for deep leagues if he sticks in the rotation for around 20 minutes a night. 

Memphis is going to be a mess, though. With 15 guys they want to play and develop, so other than Jerome, Coward, Edey, and Boozer, it's incredibly tough to project who else gets minutes.

I was happy to see Jaden McDaniels aggressive on offense, scoring 16 points and knocking down four threes. I am higher on him than most.

Kuminga stunk (and I already tweeted this last night) is not someone you need to draft in standard leagues.

The Pacers didn't play their starters much, but Aaron Nesmith had a nice game with 19 points and 4 threes. He struggled last year without Hali, but could carve out enough value to be rosterable in 12-teamers this year.

Jay Huff was awesome, too, going 16-4-2 with two stocks, and is a deep league UNICORN that shouldn't be slept on.

The Warriors played pretty much no one from their projected regular season projected rotation, so I don't care much about Dalen Terry's 23 points or Brandon Williams or Charles Bassey, yada yada

Even with Dame and Morant in the lineup, Deni Avdija put up 23 points for Portland. He and Clingan are the only early/middle round targets on this team. Dame is okay late, Morant is not someone I'm touching in 9-cat, and I've even lost my zeal for Camara after another season last year where he was just "okay." 

This rotation is also going to be a mess, but perhaps Jrue Holiday or Robert Williams will play enough for some deep league value.

author: "Thunder Dan" Palyo
text:
NBA Preseason Wednesday Night Notes

The only real situation I'm monitoring in Phoenix is Oso vs. Maluach for center minutes. Oso played 17 and started, going 8-2-2 with a steal. Maluach played 25 min off the bench, finishing with 8-7-4, no threes or blocks.  

I'm resetting expectations for Maluach a bit, but he's still the guy to roster. Oso just doesn't do much with his minutes and will always be the fifth option, no matter who he's out there with.

For the Bulls, Caleb Wilson (6-16) and Matas Buzelis (6-15) were wildly inefficient, combining to shoot 0-10 from three. It's good to see the volume there, and the shooting is bound to be better. Matas had 2 steals and 2 blocks. Still love him as a breakout, and Wilson oozes upside, but is going to have some rough nights, as all rookies do.

OKC studs looked great, and I like J-Dub for a bounceback year. Cason Wallace is a nice late-round value for steals as well. 

Aday Mara went nuts and looks tremendous, but he's just not going to play this year much unless Chet or Hartenstein are out. 

Jared McCain got up 11 shots in 16 minutes; he's still on my radar even though Ajay Mitchell is the bench guy we really want and a spot starter on nights that OKC starters are rested or hurt.

Kel'el Ware started at the four alongside Turner and had a very nice line of 18-12 with a block. Turner, FWIW, had 19-5 with 3 stocks and is a potential value late in drafts, too. 

Will they use this lineup in the regular season? They should, but even if Ware comes off the bench, he's still a breakout candidate and a target in the middle rounds.

Brayden Burries went 16-5-1 with 2 steals and is a guy I love in dynasty, though I'm not sure he'll have a large role this year unless Milwaukee moves a guard ahead of him.

The Magic starters didn't play much, other than Jase Richardson, who started for Suggs. Tristan da Silva put up a 19-5-2 line but on 6-for-16 shooting. He was solid as a fill-in last season, but isn't really draftable with Orlando at full strength.

Ty Jerome scored 17 points on 14 shots in 19 minutes. He's still a value late in drafts, but for how long? Feels like he's being touted EVERYWHERE. 

Boozer was solid with 16-6-2, while GG Jackson went off for 15 points in 13 minutes off the bench. He's a guy to keep an eye on for deep leagues if he sticks in the rotation for around 20 minutes a night. 

Memphis is going to be a mess, though. With 15 guys they want to play and develop, so other than Jerome, Coward, Edey, and Boozer, it's incredibly tough to project who else gets minutes.

I was happy to see Jaden McDaniels aggressive on offense, scoring 16 points and knocking down four threes. I am higher on him than most.

Kuminga stunk (and I already tweeted this last night) is not someone you need to draft in standard leagues.

The Pacers didn't play their starters much, but Aaron Nesmith had a nice game with 19 points and 4 threes. He struggled last year without Hali, but could carve out enough value to be rosterable in 12-teamers this year.

Jay Huff was awesome, too, going 16-4-2 with two stocks, and is a deep league UNICORN that shouldn't be slept on.

The Warriors played pretty much no one from their projected regular season projected rotation, so I don't care much about Dalen Terry's 23 points or Brandon Williams or Charles Bassey, yada yada

Even with Dame and Morant in the lineup, Deni Avdija put up 23 points for Portland. He and Clingan are the only early/middle round targets on this team. Dame is okay late, Morant is not someone I'm touching in 9-cat, and I've even lost my zeal for Camara after another season last year where he was just "okay." 

This rotation is also going to be a mess, but perhaps Jrue Holiday or Robert Williams will play enough for some deep league value.

author: Adam Stock
topic: Magic section of a multi-team post
text:
- Wagner's dimes might be for real. His assists have been up all preseason, but coming into tonight, we hadn't seen beside Suggs, so it was hard to tell if it was a role change or just due to Suggs being out. We may have got our answer tonight. Franz had 8 dimes in 22 minutes. He also had 20 points. If Wagner is a 5.0+ APG type of player this year, he's going to destroy his ADP. I already thought he was going too low before preseason started. He went in the third or fourth last year. No one thought he was overrated. Nothing has really changed since. He was crushing it before his ankle injury last year. He's still the same guy, and now he might have a larger role. He has been all over my guides and sample teams all preseason long.
- Paolo had a big night after two duds. I don't think that changes much, just like the two duds don't. He is who he is and shouldn't go anywhere close to his ADP in category leagues.
- Bane had a poor shooting night, but the usage was fine, so there's nothing to worry about there. He's a nice high-floor pick in the 50s. He's never my first pick there, but he's a nice backup option.
- Suggs has top-60 upside but comes with a ton of injury risk. I'm less concerned about him than some of the other injury-prone options due to his price. It really sucks if your third-round pick misses 30 games. If your ninth-round pick misses 30 games, it's not the end of the world.

author: "Thunder Dan" Palyo
text:
NBA Preseason Wednesday Night Notes

The only real situation I'm monitoring in Phoenix is Oso vs. Maluach for center minutes. Oso played 17 and started, going 8-2-2 with a steal. Maluach played 25 min off the bench, finishing with 8-7-4, no threes or blocks.  

I'm resetting expectations for Maluach a bit, but he's still the guy to roster. Oso just doesn't do much with his minutes and will always be the fifth option, no matter who he's out there with.

For the Bulls, Caleb Wilson (6-16) and Matas Buzelis (6-15) were wildly inefficient, combining to shoot 0-10 from three. It's good to see the volume there, and the shooting is bound to be better. Matas had 2 steals and 2 blocks. Still love him as a breakout, and Wilson oozes upside, but is going to have some rough nights, as all rookies do.

OKC studs looked great, and I like J-Dub for a bounceback year. Cason Wallace is a nice late-round value for steals as well. 

Aday Mara went nuts and looks tremendous, but he's just not going to play this year much unless Chet or Hartenstein are out. 

Jared McCain got up 11 shots in 16 minutes; he's still on my radar even though Ajay Mitchell is the bench guy we really want and a spot starter on nights that OKC starters are rested or hurt.

Kel'el Ware started at the four alongside Turner and had a very nice line of 18-12 with a block. Turner, FWIW, had 19-5 with 3 stocks and is a potential value late in drafts, too. 

Will they use this lineup in the regular season? They should, but even if Ware comes off the bench, he's still a breakout candidate and a target in the middle rounds.

Brayden Burries went 16-5-1 with 2 steals and is a guy I love in dynasty, though I'm not sure he'll have a large role this year unless Milwaukee moves a guard ahead of him.

The Magic starters didn't play much, other than Jase Richardson, who started for Suggs. Tristan da Silva put up a 19-5-2 line but on 6-for-16 shooting. He was solid as a fill-in last season, but isn't really draftable with Orlando at full strength.

Ty Jerome scored 17 points on 14 shots in 19 minutes. He's still a value late in drafts, but for how long? Feels like he's being touted EVERYWHERE. 

Boozer was solid with 16-6-2, while GG Jackson went off for 15 points in 13 minutes off the bench. He's a guy to keep an eye on for deep leagues if he sticks in the rotation for around 20 minutes a night. 

Memphis is going to be a mess, though. With 15 guys they want to play and develop, so other than Jerome, Coward, Edey, and Boozer, it's incredibly tough to project who else gets minutes.

I was happy to see Jaden McDaniels aggressive on offense, scoring 16 points and knocking down four threes. I am higher on him than most.

Kuminga stunk (and I already tweeted this last night) is not someone you need to draft in standard leagues.

The Pacers didn't play their starters much, but Aaron Nesmith had a nice game with 19 points and 4 threes. He struggled last year without Hali, but could carve out enough value to be rosterable in 12-teamers this year.

Jay Huff was awesome, too, going 16-4-2 with two stocks, and is a deep league UNICORN that shouldn't be slept on.

The Warriors played pretty much no one from their projected regular season projected rotation, so I don't care much about Dalen Terry's 23 points or Brandon Williams or Charles Bassey, yada yada

Even with Dame and Morant in the lineup, Deni Avdija put up 23 points for Portland. He and Clingan are the only early/middle round targets on this team. Dame is okay late, Morant is not someone I'm touching in 9-cat, and I've even lost my zeal for Camara after another season last year where he was just "okay." 

This rotation is also going to be a mess, but perhaps Jrue Holiday or Robert Williams will play enough for some deep league value.

text:

text:
What I learned in NBA last night

1) Giannis putting up 35.6 points, 17 rebounds & 15 assists per 100 possessions in preseason so far. Possible career year ahead. Will be more motivated than any year since his title. Moved to +1000 for MVP last 2 days. 

2) Cade Cunningham controlled the game against the Timberwolves after a slow start. Still only 25 years old & somehow being overlooked. Pistons won’t win 60 games in a crowded east, but John Collins & Isaiah Joe give them scalable scoring depth. 

3) Pelicans guard Jeremiah Fears will have a great 2nd season. He turned 20 years old yesterday & has future all-star tools. Knocking down 54% of his threes in preseason. Averaged 37 ppg in his final 3 games last season. He’s +8000 for most improved player & +10000 for 6th man. 

4) Jonathan Kuminga gives this Timberwolves rotation 5 legit scoring options. His team friendly contract will be one of the league’s best if he stays healthy. One of the sneakiest pickups of the entire offseason. 

5) The Celtics will have one of the best defensive frontcourts in the league with Mitchell Robinson & reserve Neemias Queta. Will be a nightmare for opposing teams. Joe Mazzulla experimented with a double big lineup with them late last night, looked promising. 

6) Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. was solid in his preseason debut against the Heat. He has a truly dynamic skillset that translates to the pro game. Had durability issues, but he’ll have every opportunity to accelerate his development with the Nets. He’s +4000 for rookie of the year. 

7) Jalen Duren was dominant in his matchup against Rudy Gobert. 24 points in only 15 minutes. Wreaked havoc defensively as well. He’ll be judged by what he does in the postseason after disappearing against the Magic, but has a great chance to change the narrative. Still only 22 years old.

author: Myguyknowsaguy
text:
What I learned in NBA last night 

1) Darryn Peterson thriving in preseason after a slow start in opener. Jazz already running sets for him as a playmaker & he looks effective in transition. Doesn’t look like a rookie. Currently +350 for ROTY.

2) Heathy Trae Young with 12.1 assists per 36 minutes in preseason so far. Meshing well with his Wizards teammates. Plenty of lob & transition targets for him as well. He’s currently +340 to lead the league in assists, 2nd behind Jokic. 

3) OKC Thunder rookie Bennett Stirtz is proving his draft doubters wrong. Leads the team in preseason with 20.3 ppg, 4.3 ast & 4.7 rebounds, while knocking down 59% of his threes. GM Sam Presti is the best talent evaluator in the league & I wouldn’t be surprised to see Stirtz enter the rotation in year one. 

4) Nets star Michael Porter Jr. is rolling in preseason. Julius Randle excelled as a playmaker in their win against the Wizards, had 8 assists before halftime. They have complimentary skillsets and could form an surprisingly effective duo in a crowded eastern conference. 

5) Anthony Edwards is 100% healthy & thriving off-ball when LaMelo Ball is on the court. His current level of aggression in preseason foreshadows what will likely be a career scoring year. Timberwolves are clearly emphasizing playing at a faster pace this season. This team will be electric. Their season win total is currently set at 46.5. Ant is +1600 for MVP.

author: Myguyknowsaguy
text:
NBA preseason opens up tomorrow with the Heat taking on my Raptors. I’m very high on Toronto this season with Kawhi returning. Key driver will be the continued development of Scottie Barnes, he displayed all-world potential in that 1st round matchup vs the Cavs, he dominated his matchup against Evan Mobley and was the best player on the floor in that series. 

Raptors are around +2200 to win the title now after hovering around +4500 when the Leonard Clippers trade was uncertain in the summer. The east will be a gauntlet this year, but they have a legit chance at breaking through. I think they’ll eventually have the best defense in the east. Look out for CMB, Ja’Kobe Walter & Jamal Shead, all of whom made legit strides last season. 

Miami is a very interesting team. Currently around +3500 to win the title. Surrounding Giannis with players that can stretch the floor consistently has been a successful recipe for years. Adding Klay Thompson & Tim Hardaway Jr. should pay off. 

Trading Kel’el Ware was disappointing, he’s a very promising young talent, but they wanted to accelerate their competitive timeline & getting Bobby Portis back in the Giannis trade was big.

I’m expecting a big leap from Pelle Larsson this season, a player that exceeded his contract value by a significant margin last season. 

This Heat team can make some noise this season in a crowded eastern conference. Erik Spoelstra should be able to manage Giannis effectively.

I don’t think Kawhi will play in the preseason opener tomorrow, but Giannis should start. The journey begins.

Coulibaly was great off the bench with 19-2-1 and 4 stocks. He and Tre Johnson are probably going to play enough to be in the conversation for standard leagues.

author: Adam Stock
topic: Wizards section of a multi-team post
text:
- No AD tonight so there were some extra shots up for grabs. Dynbantsa was so-so, but he did have a steal and a block. He needs to surprise in the defensive categories to be more than a back-end player. The steals have been there so far. He's not someone I'm too interested in because he's ranked at his ceiling. 
- George was very impressive yet again. He had 21 on 7 shots, three triples, 6-6 from the line, four dimes, and three steals in just 25 minutes. He is the late-round guy I've done a big 180 on this preseason. I don't think he was in any of my sample teams the first time around. He was in a bunch in today's update. I'll be going after him late. I do think 30+ MPG is very possible this year. It's not like the Wizards have anyone too interesting on their bench.
- Sarr was very quiet again. He's going to start slow. He just returned from a major injury and has to get used to playing beside AD. Big upside, but he does feel a little risky. 
- Ayton started for AD. He'll be one of those guys who gets picked up and then dropped a dozen times this year. A very nice stream whenever one of the starting bigs is out but not a long-term hold.

author: Adam Stock
topic: Wizards section of a multi-team post
text:
- AD's debut for the Wizards went very well. He looked like his usual self. He's pretty tempting in round 2. I would definitely think about it. I like him more than most of the injury-prone guys because when healthy, he can help the teams built around the later first-round picks compete with teams built around the big boys. I'd stay away if I landed one of the top four. You have a championship ceiling in that scenario. You don't need to take a major swing. If your first-round pick is someone like Ant or Johnson, you do need to take some swings at some point. 
- Dybantsa had four steals in 23 minutes. He had a bad steal rate in college, so for now I would assume this was a fluke performance. He's just a final-round flier to me in both category and points leagues.
- Kyshawn started and looked pretty good. 12/7/5 with a block and two threes in 22 minutes. It's hard to see how he picks up enough usage to be more than a back-end player, but I would still draft him. I like the talent, and his game is fantasy-friendly. 
- Ayton started for Sarr, who is expected to be back for the opener. We don't need to draft him anywhere, but Ayton will be a grab whenever one of the starting bigs is out, which could be a fair amount.
